summary: Tank kneels beside Morpheus's body, mourning him, and reaches for the plug to kill Morpheus, but Neo shouts 'Stop!' and refuses to accept his death, insisting the Oracle told him he would have to make a choice. Neo decides to re-enter the Matrix to rescue Morpheus, confessing to Trinity that he is not the One, which stuns her. Tank argues the rescue is suicide against three Agents in a military building, but Neo says he must go because he now believes in something: that he can bring Morpheus back. Trinity then declares she is coming too, asserting her authority as ranking officer, and orders Tank to load them up.

what_changes.before: Paralyzed by the finality of the moment, Neo is frozen as Tank prepares to pull the plug on Morpheus.
what_changes.after: Neo finds decisive purpose, choosing to re-enter the Matrix to save Morpheus.
what_changes.evidence: He makes his choice. Turning, he walks to his chair. TRINITY What are you doing? NEO I'm going in.

what_changes.before: Neo had believed, or let others believe, that he might be the One.
what_changes.after: Neo explicitly renounces being the One, telling Trinity the Oracle confirmed he is not.
what_changes.evidence: NEO I'm not the One, Trinity. The Oracle hit me with that, too. ... I'm sorry, I'm not. I'm just another guy.

what_changes.before: Trinity is overcome with grief and tries to stop Neo, insisting Morpheus sacrificed himself so Neo could get out.
what_changes.after: Trinity commits to joining Neo's suicide mission, asserting her rank to override his objections.
what_changes.evidence: Her jaw sets and she starts climbing into the chair beside him. ... 'since I am the ranking officer on this ship, if you don't like it then I believe that you can go to hell'

what_changes.before: Tank is resolved to kill Morpheus, saying 'this has to be done' and that they cannot let Zion fall.
what_changes.after: Tank shifts to preparing to help Neo and Trinity re-enter, obeying Trinity's order to load them up.
what_changes.evidence: TANK Neo, this is loco. ... what you are talking about is suicide. ... [ends with] TRINITY Tank, load us up.

event_hint.kind: a wake turned into a rescue decision
event_hint.one_line: During the mourning of Morpheus, Neo reverses the crew's plan to kill him and instead resolves to re-enter the Matrix to rescue him, with Trinity and Tank falling in behind.

uncertain: What the Oracle actually told Neo about the choice, since Neo only partially reveals it.
Whether Trinity truly believes Neo can succeed or is following him despite her doubt.

minds.wants: To stop the crew from killing Morpheus and to seize the only action left — re-entering the Matrix to bring Morpheus back.
minds.feels: A sudden, almost physical clarity ("sees it perfectly clear, fate rushing at him like an oncoming train") that resolves his earlier paralysis into purpose. Underneath the certainty is a man who has just surrendered the identity everyone built around him — he is not the One — and found that the surrender does not destroy him but frees him to act for a reason that is now his own, not borrowed from prophecy.
minds.shows: Outrage first ("Goddamnit!"), then a hard, quiet decisiveness. He lets them see the renunciation of being the One — "I'm just another guy" — but he does NOT let them see why he is truly sure the rescue isn't suicide: "I can't logically explain to you why it's not." He shows belief where he cannot show logic.
minds.basis: His "Stop!" interrupts Tank at the plug; his walk to the chair; the confession to Trinity that the Oracle told him he's not the One; and "I believe I can bring him back," which he admits he cannot justify logically. The paralysis-then-motion beat is the visible pivot.

believes_about.belief: That Morpheus's willingness to die for a belief is something Neo now finally understands and must honor by acting the same way.
believes_about.wrong_because: Neo believes he has understood Morpheus's faith, but he has only just adopted it; he cannot yet know that acting on it will transform him into the very thing he just denied being.

believes_about.belief: That telling Trinity he is not the One will relieve her of the burden of his supposed destiny and let her accept that Morpheus is "the one that matters."
believes_about.wrong_because: He misreads how deeply her commitment is tied to him, not to the prophecy — she does not abandon him when the prophecy is removed, which is the opposite of what his logic predicts.

minds.wants: First to keep Neo from going back; then, once she cannot stop him, to bind herself to him and take command of the mission so she is not left behind.
minds.feels: Grief already present ("tears slip free"), then a shock that is less about Morpheus than about Neo dismantling the meaning she has lived by. When she cannot answer his "Why?" — "Uncertainty swallows her words" — she is confronted with the possibility that her faith was in a man, not in a prophecy. She converts that vertigo into authority.
minds.shows: She shows shock ("stunned"), a reflexive denial ("No, you... have to be"), and then, decisively, the set jaw and the climb into the chair. What she does NOT show is the thing she "wants to tell him" and cannot — whatever that feeling is, she masks it as rank and duty: "if you don't like it then I believe that you can go to hell."
minds.basis: Her progression from stopping him, to stunned denial of his non-One confession, to being unable to explain why he must be the One, to seizing the officer's prerogative to join him. The script explicitly flags the unsaid.

believes_about.belief: That he must be the One, so his self-renunciation cannot be true ("It can't be true").
believes_about.wrong_because: Her belief that he is the One is exactly what Neo has just told her is false, and the coming events will test which of them was right — she is holding a belief partly because losing it is unbearable, not because of evidence in the moment.

believes_about.belief: That he is "just another guy" who needs her help and rank to survive the mission.
believes_about.wrong_because: She believes she is protecting a capable but ordinary man; she cannot yet see that the belief he has just discovered in himself is the beginning of the power that will make him extraordinary.

minds.wants: To carry out the grim necessity of killing Morpheus to protect Zion — then, once overruled, to keep his comrades alive by loading them for a mission he is certain will kill them.
minds.feels: Freshly bereaved — he has just covered his dead brother (sc-146) and called Morpheus a father — so pulling the plug is unbearable to him personally even as he insists it "has to be done." His grief and his duty are at war, and duty wins out loud while grief works underneath.
minds.shows: The eulogy, the grip on the plug, and the practical objection to the rescue ("this is loco... suicide. Three of them!"). He shows reasoned resistance, not the raw loss driving it. He ends by obeying the ranking officer without further argument.
minds.basis: His eulogy to Morpheus as "a father," his "this has to be done" and Zion-over-all argument in sc-146 and here, and his tactical enumeration of why the rescue is suicide. He submits to "Tank, load us up."

believes_about.belief: That Neo's plan is emotional, illogical suicide born of a kid refusing to accept a death.
believes_about.wrong_because: He reads Neo's resolve as desperation, not as the first genuine, self-authored conviction Neo has ever acted on — the distinction that will make the impossible rescue succeed.

believes_about.belief: That her authority as ranking officer is a legitimate and sufficient reason to join and command the mission.
believes_about.wrong_because: Unstated in the scene, but his immediate compliance suggests he accepts the rank claim at face value; what he cannot know is that her real motive is Neo, not chain of command.

minds.wants: Nothing legible — he is unconscious and being interrogated; he is an object here, not an agent.
minds.feels: Not available; he is absent from the active mind of the scene.
minds.shows: Nothing; his body is what the others act around.
minds.basis: The scene gives him no action, reaction, or decision — he is the corpse-to-be and the stated reason for the others' choices. Per instruction, no inner life is invented to fill the field.

connects_back: Tank's decision in sc-146 to pull the plug to keep Zion's codes from the Agents, and his covering of his dead brother, which makes this mourning personal.
Trinity's relentless pacing and rage at Cypher's betrayal in sc-146, the grief she is still carrying into this moment.
The Oracle's earlier prophecy to Neo (prior scenes) that he would "have to make a choice," which he now interprets as this moment and only partially reveals.
Morpheus's interrogation by the Agents in sc-145 and sc-147, the live pressure that makes every second of the rescue a race against the codes being extracted.
Neo's prior uncertainty about whether he is the One, which crystallizes here into explicit renunciation.
sets_up: The debate over the rescue's viability and the crew's commitment to the suicide mission (ev-026).
The two-person assault on the government building — lobby firefight, elevator rigged as a bomb, counterweight climb to the roof (ev-027).
The helicopter extraction of Morpheus from the interrogation office (ev-028).
The rooftop regroup and the subway escape that follows (ev-029, ev-030).
Neo's emerging self-belief, which will be tested and grown in his solo confrontation with Agent Smith (ev-031).
dramatic_function: This is the scene that converts grief and fatalism into agency. It reverses the crew's accepted ending (kill Morpheus) into an impossible beginning (rescue him), and it relocates the story's engine from external prophecy to internal belief — Neo acts not because he is the One but because he chooses to believe, which is precisely the faith that will make him the One. It also re-anchors the trio (Neo, Trinity, Morpheus) and re-establishes Trinity's authority and devotion as the force that ensures Neo is not alone.
